newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec unveils C$250 million tax to fight poverty.
newsitem.headline: Quebec unveils C$250 million tax to fight poverty.

text.p: Quebec Finance Minister Bernard Landry unveiled Tuesday a C$250 million tax to fight poverty that will be phased out over the next three years.
The measure, which was approved last month at a province-wide economic summit, will equal 0.3 percent of the income tax paid by individuals.
Corporations operating in Quebec will be required to pay up to 2.8 percent of their income tax. Financial institutions will have to pay 3 percent of their capital.
The tax will be implemented over three years. It will go to a fund that puts money into measures to encourage individuals to return to the labor market.
Landry promised the tax would be abolished in three years. "I am firmly committed to that," he said.
